$comment: cna-template renderer manifest — the ONE place template-side renderer metadata lives.
This file does NOT own the list of renderer names. CNA does, in
cna/cmake/RendererSelection.cmake (the set_property(CACHE CNA_GRAPHICS_RENDERER
PROPERTY STRINGS ...) line). cmake/CnaRenderers.cmake reads that list out of the
CNA checkout at configure time and cross-checks it against the names below, so a
renderer added to CNA cannot silently go missing here — the configure fails with a
drift error naming the exact renderers that differ.
What this file DOES own is the metadata CNA does not expose programmatically:
which platforms a renderer is valid on, whether it needs a display to run, what it
depends on, and how cna-template's presets/CI/docs should treat it.
Fields:
platforms   Target platforms on which this renderer is supported. Derived from
the gates in cna/cmake/RendererSelection.cmake plus CNA's own
support statements. 'linux'|'windows'|'macos'|'web'|'android'.
experimental Platforms CNA does not gate but does not support either. The
template warns rather than failing, so you can still try them.
gate        How CNA enforces it: 'fatal' (hard FATAL_ERROR), 'warn' (builds
elsewhere but warns), 'none' (no platform gate at all).
category    Renderer family, used to group docs and to pick CI representatives.
dimension   '2d' = 2D only, '2d3d' = 2D and 3D.
display     'window' = needs a real or virtual display to RUN, 'none' = runs
with no display at all (usable as-is in CI).
dependency  What it needs beyond CNA + SDL3 + sharp-runtime.
tier        cna-template CI tier: 'B' = every PR, 'C' = broad matrix,
'D' = scheduled/manual only, 'X' = not runnable on GitHub runners.
preset      Whether a named convenience preset is generated for it.
webflags    Extra Emscripten link options this renderer needs (web only).
notes       Short user-facing note.
Regenerate presets + docs after editing:  python3 tools/gen_renderer_files.py
Check for drift without writing:          python3 tools/gen_renderer_files.py --check

renderers.name: SDL_RENDERER
renderers.notes: Most portable renderer, and CNA's default off Linux. 2D only: no VertexBuffer/IndexBuffer/depth buffer. CNA documents it as untested on the web -- use WEBGL2 or CANVAS there.

renderers.name: SDL_GPU
renderers.notes: SDL3's own GPU abstraction. Needs libshaderc installed (libshaderc-dev).

renderers.name: OPENGLES3
renderers.notes: CNA's default renderer on Linux. Internally EasyGL.

renderers.name: OPENGLES2
renderers.notes: Internally EasyGL, GLES 2.0 profile. Cannot target the web — use WEBGL1.

renderers.name: OPENGL33
renderers.notes: Internally EasyGL, desktop GL 3.3 core profile.

renderers.name: WEBGL2
renderers.notes: CNA's default renderer under Emscripten. Internally EasyGL.

renderers.name: WEBGL1
renderers.notes: WebGL 1 profile. Forcing MAX_WEBGL_VERSION=2 globally would break this.

renderers.name: OPENGL1
renderers.notes: Legacy fixed-function OpenGL 1.x. Desktop Linux/Windows only.

renderers.name: OPENGL2
renderers.notes: Desktop OpenGL 2.1 compatibility profile, GLSL 1.10. No EasyGL.

renderers.name: OPENGL4
renderers.notes: Real desktop OpenGL 4.x core profile, independent of EasyGL.

renderers.name: OPENGLES1
renderers.notes: OpenGL ES 1.1 fixed-function. Needs a real GLESv1_CM system library.

renderers.name: VULKAN
renderers.notes: Real 3D via Vulkan. Builds on a CI runner but needs a real or software ICD to run.

renderers.name: WEBGPU
renderers.notes: Despite the name this is a NATIVE renderer; CNA rejects it under Emscripten.

renderers.name: METAL
renderers.notes: macOS only. iOS/tvOS explicitly unvalidated upstream.

renderers.name: HEADLESS
renderers.notes: No GPU and no window at all. The right choice for CI and servers.

renderers.name: SOFTWARE
renderers.notes: Real CPU rasterizer. Creates no window and does not link SDL3, so Present() puts nothing on screen -- it is a compute/test renderer, not a display one.

renderers.name: STUB
renderers.notes: Deliberate no-op renderer. Draws nothing, touches no GPU or window.

renderers.name: PORTABLEGL
renderers.notes: CPU OpenGL 3.x-style pipeline. Links no SDL3 and needs no display at all.

renderers.name: TINYGL
renderers.notes: CPU fixed-function OpenGL 1.x subset. Links no SDL3 and needs no display at all.

renderers.name: SKIA
renderers.dependency: a Skia you built yourself (CNA_SKIA_ROOT + CNA_SKIA_BUILD_DIR)
renderers.notes: Skia is never fetched: CNA fails configure unless you point it at your own build.

renderers.name: BLEND2D
renderers.notes: Blend2D CPU vector rasterizer, presented through an SDL texture.

renderers.name: OPENVG
renderers.notes: OpenVG 1.1 vector graphics on a fixed-function desktop GL context.

renderers.name: CANVAS
renderers.notes: Browser 2D canvas context. Needs no WebGL at all.

renderers.name: HTML_DOM
renderers.notes: Draws sprites as pooled CSS-transformed <div> elements. No WebGL.

renderers.name: SVG_DOM
renderers.notes: Draws sprites as real <svg>/<image> elements. No WebGL.

renderers.name: PIXIJS
renderers.notes: PixiJS retained-mode WebGL scene graph for SpriteBatch and render targets.

renderers.name: BGFX
renderers.notes: bgfx cross-platform renderer. Primarily tested on Linux upstream.

renderers.name: MAGNUM
renderers.notes: Desktop GL through Magnum's typed wrappers. Cannot target the web.

renderers.name: WICKED
renderers.dependency: Wicked Engine (CNA_WICKED_ROOT; auto-fetch is OFF by default)
renderers.notes: Dispatches to Vulkan or D3D12. Configure fails unless you supply CNA_WICKED_ROOT.

renderers.name: SOKOL
renderers.dependency: sokol single header via FetchContent + system OpenGL
renderers.notes: Adds CNA_SOKOL_API (GLCORE default; only GLCORE is verified upstream).

renderers.name: DILIGENT
renderers.notes: Diligent picks D3D11/D3D12/Vulkan/GL/Metal at runtime.

renderers.name: LLGL
renderers.notes: LLGL picks OpenGL or Vulkan at runtime. Needs libshaderc installed.

renderers.name: IGL
renderers.dependency: facebook/igl v1.1.1 plus selected bootstrap dependencies
renderers.notes: Meta IGL with CNA's verified Linux OpenGL/GLX and Vulkan backends.

renderers.name: FNA3D
renderers.dependency: FNA3D + MojoShader via FetchContent; needs Python3
renderers.notes: The XNA-shaped C library FNA renders through. Picks SDL_GPU/D3D11/GL at runtime.

renderers.name: NANOVG
renderers.notes: NanoVG vector graphics through its desktop OpenGL 2 backend.

renderers.name: FREEDIRECT
renderers.notes: DirectDraw reimplemented on SDL3, so unlike DIRECTX* it builds on Linux.

renderers.name: GDI
renderers.notes: Classic Win32 GDI, 2D only.

renderers.name: GLIDE
renderers.notes: 3dfx Glide 3.x. Requires a 32-bit (i686) Windows toolchain.

renderers.name: DIRECT2D
renderers.notes: Direct2D 1.1, 2D only.

renderers.name: DIRECTX11
renderers.notes: Direct3D 11.

renderers.name: DIRECTX12
renderers.notes: Direct3D 12.

renderers.name: DIRECTX10
renderers.dependency: d3d10 (delivered via Wine + DXVK d3d10core when cross-testing)
renderers.notes: Direct3D 10. Shader-only pipeline: every draw needs real HLSL vs_4_0/ps_4_0.

renderers.name: DIRECTX9
renderers.notes: Direct3D 9.

renderers.name: DIRECTX8
renderers.dependency: DXVK d3d8 import library via CNA_DX8_DXVK_LIB (mingw-w64 ships none)
renderers.notes: Direct3D 8, fixed-function only. DirectDraw no longer exists at this era.

renderers.name: DIRECTX7
renderers.notes: DirectDraw 7 + Direct3D 7. Viewport objects removed at this era.

renderers.name: DIRECTX6
renderers.notes: Same interfaces as DIRECTX5; adds real stencil buffer operations.

renderers.name: DIRECTX5
renderers.notes: First era with no execute buffers: FVF DrawPrimitive only.

renderers.name: DIRECTX3
renderers.notes: Real DirectX 3. Not to be confused with FREEDIRECT, which once held this name.

renderers.name: DIRECTX2
renderers.notes: DirectDraw v1 + Direct3D v2 DrawPrimitive.

renderers.name: DIRECTX1
renderers.notes: Real DirectDraw v1. No Direct3D at this era.
